question: is there a screenwriting concentration

body.answer:
Yes. The Filmmaking BA (Bachelor of Arts) includes a Screenwriting Concentration, requiring FILM 344 WRITING THE SCREENPLAY and FILM 391 TV WRITERS' ROOM. [13]

Sources: [13](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

Ramapo’s catalog lists a Crime and Justice Studies minor, not a criminology major. [1] Criminology is included among the disciplines informing the Law and Society major, and students in Law and Society can pursue a Criminal Justice concentration or the Crime and Justice Studies minor. [7][9] You could contact the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office to ask about your options. [7]

**School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7625; (201) 684-7562. Email: SSSWOffice@ramapo.edu. Office: ASB-431. [15]

answer:
Ramapo’s catalog lists a Crime and Justice Studies minor, not a criminology major. [7][9] You could contact the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office to ask about your options. [7]

answer:
No. The catalog lists no bachelor’s major in Creative Writing. It lists a Creative Writing Minor and a Creative Writing Concentration within the English & Literary Studies BA, including a Teacher Education Track with that concentration. [14] The English and Literary Studies page also says students may minor or concentrate in Creative Writing. [9]

body.answer:
Yes. Photography Concentration is in the Visual Arts BA (Bachelor of Arts). [20] Requirements: choose at least 1 of ARTS 101 FUNDAMENTALS OF DRAWING or ARTS 201 BASIC PAINTING; take ARTS 202 BASIC SCULPTURE, ARTS 207 DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY, and ARTS 211 BASIC ART & TECHNOLOGY; complete ARHT 204 INTRODUCTION TO GLOBAL ART TRADITIONS and ARHT 245 MASTERPIECES IN WESTERN CIVILIZATION, plus 1 additional required 300-level Art History (ARHT) Course; choose 1 Arts Upper-level Elective from the listed options; take ARHT 214 PHOTOGRAPHY CONCEPTS AND HISTORIES and ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY; choose at least 3 Photography Electives: ARTS 312 INTERMEDIATE FILM PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 315 MEDIUM AND LARGE FORMAT PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 318 INTERMEDIATE DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 324 DOCUMENTARY PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 328 PORTRAIT PHOTOGRAPHY, or ARTS 406 ADVANCED PHOTOGRAPHY; take CNTP 388 CO-OP/INTERNSHIP CONTEMPORARY ARTS and ARTS 408 SENIOR THESIS EXHIBITION. [1]
ARTS 207 DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY is 4 credits; no published prerequisites. [3] ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY is 4 credits, has no published prerequisites, and carries Gen Ed 18-Culture & Creativity (GECC). [4] ARTS 312 INTERMEDIATE FILM PHOTOGRAPHY is 4 credits; Prerequisite Prerequisite Course complete all of: - ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY. [5] ARTS 315 MEDIUM AND LARGE FORMAT PHOTOGRAPHY is 4 credits; Prerequisite Prerequisite Course complete all of: - ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY. [7] ARTS 318 INTERMEDIATE DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY is 4 credits; Prerequisite Prerequisite Course complete all of: - ARTS 207 DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY. [6] ARTS 324 DOCUMENTARY PHOTOGRAPHY is 4 credits; Prerequisite Select 1 Course complete one of: - ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY - ARTS 207 DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY. [8]

All existing academic programs that alter courses and/or requirements will follow the approval procedures outlined in the ARC Manual.
All existing undergraduate academic programs will undergo a regularly scheduled cycle of program review and student-learning assessment including, but not limited to, the review and use of assessment data to improve student learning.
All existing graduate programs will undergo an annual review of enrollment, revenue, and expenses, as well as an annual cycle of student-learning assessment.
All academic programs will meet the definitions and/or stipulations provided in the sections below.
Undergraduate Degree Programs
An undergraduate degree program consists of the General Education program, a major, and free electives. Students have the option to pursue a minor and/or a second major.
General Education: The hallmark of a liberal-arts education, the General Education program must provide students the opportunity to acquire competency in at least communication (both written and oral), reasoning (both scientific and quantitative), critical thinking and analysis, and technology. The General Education curriculum should not exceed 41 credits.
Students may double count courses in the General Education curriculum and the major. A single course may not fulfill two separate General Education competencies, and no more than two General Education courses may double count in the General Education curriculum and the major. The catalog lists two film bachelor’s majors: Filmmaking BA and Theater and Film BA [12]. The Filmmaking BA requirements name courses but do not give a total credit count for the major [1]. Ramapo requires 128 credits to graduate, but program credit requirements differ; review the number of classes and credits with your adviser [5]. Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising).

question: how many credits to graduate w a nursing degree

body.answer:
For an undergraduate nursing degree, you need a minimum of 128 credits to graduate [6]. The Registrar says at least 32 credits must be completed at Ramapo, and recommends reviewing the number of classes and credits with your adviser [5]. Nursing majors must also meet the 2.3 GPA requirement [7].

For the Nursing MSN, the catalog lists courses rather than a total credit count [1]. The MSN curriculum page says the degree consists of 34/35 credits with a 135 hour Role Practicum [14]. An older catalog-based program requirement likewise lists courses, not a program total [1].

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MSN-NURM) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/msn/curriculum/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
For an undergraduate nursing degree, you need a minimum of 128 credits to graduate [6]. The Registrar says at least 32 credits must be completed at Ramapo, and recommends reviewing the number of classes and credits with your adviser [5]. Nursing majors must also meet the 2.3 GPA requirement [7].

For the Nursing MSN, the catalog lists courses rather than a total credit count [1]. The MSN curriculum page says the degree consists of 34/35 credits with a 135 hour Role Practicum [14]. An older catalog-based program requirement likewise lists courses, not a program total [1].

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [15]
